newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-SAMPRAS BEATS KAFELNIKOV TO EARN PLACE IN SWISS FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS BEATS KAFELNIKOV TO EARN PLACE IN SWISS FINAL.

text.p: U.S Open champion Pete Sampras gained a measure of revenge for his defeat by eventual winner Yevgeny Kafelnikov in the French Open with a 7-6 6-3 win over the Russian in the Swiss indoor championship on Saturday.

While Sampras had won four of the six meetings between the pair, Kafelnikov had taken the last two, including a straight sets semifinal win at the French Open earlier this year to deny the American a shot at the only grand slam title to elude him.
Sampras will meet Germany's Hendrik Dreekman in Sunday's final.
Dreekmann, looking for first career title, breezed into his second final of the season with a 7-5 6-4 win over the Czech Republic's Jiri Novak.
Sampras will be going after the 43rd title of his career.

Playing in his first tournament since winning a fourth U.S. Open, the 25-year-old American will also be looking to keep his 100 per cent record intact, having won all six finals he has appeared in this year.
Sampras said later the key to reaching his seventh final was surviving the a tense first set which he won in a tie-break 7-4.
Kafelnikov, the third seed and world number five, took early control as he broke Sampras to go in to a 3-0 lead.
But Sampras broke back and held serve to pull even at 4-4, the set going to the tie-break when Kafelnikov failed to convert a match point at 6-5.
Sampras had the only break in the second set to go ahead 3-1 and never gave the Russian an opportunity to break back, wrapping up the match in one hour 13 minutes.

"It wasn't easy, it could have gone either way," said Sampras, the first number one to play in the Swiss indoors since Bjorn Borg in 1980. "He had set point once and he could have won the first set just as easily.
"He got off to a good start but you have to keep on plugging away and hope to get a break, which I did.
"The second set I saw him hang his head a little and I took advantage of it."
Timely back-to-back breaks were also the key to Dreekmann's semifinal win over Novak, who had upset Australian Open champion Boris Becker in the second round on Thursday.
Dreekmann, ranked 49th in the world, broke late in the first set to go up 6-5 and then serve out for the set.
The German began the second set with another break and then held serve to win the first meeting between the two promising 21-year-olds.
"He's obviously got to this stage by playing good tennis," said Sampras. "He's had a good run but hopefully it will end tomorrow."
